description: Hi! I’m Reva, an Electronics & Computer Science student from Mumbai. I enjoy building projects in Python, MATLAB, and web development, with an interest in AI and satellite data analysis. We’re forming a team for NASA Space Apps 2026 and looking for teammates skilled in data science, ai. Beginners are welcome if you’re curious and eager to collaborate.
summary:
Mars Nav is an interactive web we developed for NASA’s “Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map” challenge. Users start from a cinematic 3D Mars globe, zoom into Jezero Crater, pick a start and end point on 2D or 3D terrain, and instantly get a mission report with route distance, travel time, difficulty and resources.

It addresses the challenge by combining NASA open data, including terrain slope, thermal inertia, radiation, wind and temperature, CRISM minerals and Perseverance rover images, into a single map that shows where travel on Mars is safe and what to expect along the way.

This matters because Mars exploration is risky and communication delays make careful planning essential. Mars Nav helps astronauts and mission planners make safer, faster decisions, and it makes complex space data easy for students and the public to understand.
details:
Mars Nav helps users plan safe routes across Mars. It starts with a cinematic 3D Mars globe, then lets users zoom into Jezero Crater, pick a start and end point on 2D or 3D terrain, and instantly receive a mission report with route distance, travel time, difficulty and resources. It works by combining NASA open data, including terrain slope, thermal inertia, radiation, wind and temperature, CRISM minerals and Perseverance rover images, into one map that highlights hazards along the way.

The benefits are safer and faster route planning, and clear visuals that turn complex space data into something anyone can understand. The intended impact is to support future astronauts and mission planners, and to inspire students by making NASA open data accessible.

We built it with React, Vite, Three.js, Leaflet, Framer Motion and a backend API, using HiRISE, CTX elevation, THEMIS and CRISM data. It is creative through its immersive intro animation, COSMO-style dashboard and smooth switching between 2D and 3D views. Our team considered scientific accuracy, terrain and radiation safety, ease of use and reliable backend integration.
